e-493.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
e-493.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot (2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(2{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{(e)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-2{(1)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})]-6{\int }_{1}^{e}x\text{d}x \\  & =6{e}^{2}-6(\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3{x}^{2}{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3({e}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

e-494.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
e-494.worked_solution:
We define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

e-3993.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
e-3993.worked_solution:
At first, it may not look like we have two factors. Actually, we do, but one of them is implicit. The trick is to write the integral as

$$
\int \ln{x}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln{x} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x.
$$

 

Using this trick, we can now use integration by parts. We let

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the by-parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=x^{-1/2}dx gives du=dx/x and v=2√x. Thus the integral is 2√x ln(x)−2∫x^{-1/2}dx=2√x ln(x)−4√x+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x=2\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(2\sqrt{x})-\int (2\sqrt{x})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-4\sqrt{x}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Question 1
?

∫ln⁡xxdx=

a
2xln⁡x−6xx−4x+C
b
2xln⁡x−4x+C
c
2xln⁡x−4x−6x+C
d
2xln⁡x−4xx+C
e
2xln⁡x+6xx−4x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(x)⟹u′=1xv′=1x⟹v=∫1xdx=2x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫ln⁡xxdx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡x(2x)−∫(2x)(1x)dx=2xln⁡(x)−2∫1xdx=2xln⁡(x)−4x+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x=2\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(2\sqrt{x})-\int (2\sqrt{x})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-4\sqrt{x}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Question 2
?

∫2xln⁡(x2)dx=

a
x(ln⁡(x2)−1)+C
b
x2(ln⁡(x)−1)+C
c
x22(ln⁡(x)+2)+C
d
x2(ln⁡(x2)−1)+C
e
x22(ln⁡(x2)−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x²) and dv=2x dx gives du=(2/x)dx and v=x². Therefore the integral is x²ln(x²)−∫2x dx=x²(ln(x²)−1)+C, which is option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot {x}^{2}-\int {x}^{2}(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-2\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-{x}^{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot {x}^{2}-\int {x}^{2}(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-2\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-{x}^{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives an antiderivative (2/3)x⁶ln(x)−x⁶/9. Evaluating at e³ and 1 gives 2e¹⁸−e¹⁸/9+1/9=(17e¹⁸+1)/9.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4{x}^{5} & \,⟹\,v=\int 4{x}^{5}\,dx=\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}4{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}(\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{2({e}^{3})^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})}{3}-\frac{2(1)^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{3}]-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{18}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})}{3}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{9}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =2{e}^{18}-(\frac{{e}^{18}}{9}-\frac{1}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(18{e}^{18}-{e}^{18}+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(17{e}^{18}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

∫(x+7)ln⁡xdx=

a
x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x24−7x+C
b
x2ln⁡x2+7ln⁡x+x24−7x+C
c
xln⁡x2−7ln⁡x−x24+7x+C
d
x2ln⁡x2−7ln⁡x−x24−7x2+C
e
xln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x4−7x2+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Use integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=(x+7)dx, so du=dx/x and v=x²/2+7x. The integral equals (x²/2+7x)ln(x)−∫(x/2+7)dx=x²ln(x)/2+7xln(x)−x²/4−7x+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x+7\, & ⟹\,v=\int (x+7)\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x-7\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-7x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡x⟹u′=1xv′=x+7⟹v=∫(x+7)dx=x22+7x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(x+7)ln⁡xdx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡x(x22+7x)−∫(x22+7x)(1x)dx=x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−12∫xdx−7∫dx=x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x24−7x+C, where C is an integral constant.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a. Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and v=x²/2+7x gives (x²/2+7x)ln(x)−∫(x/2+7)dx=x²ln(x)/2+7xln(x)−x²/4−7x+C. Its derivative is (x+7)ln(x).

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x+7\, & ⟹\,v=\int (x+7)\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x-7\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-7x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4{x}^{6} & \,⟹\,v=\int 4{x}^{6}\,dx=\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}4{x}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}(\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{4({e}^{2})^{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{7}-\frac{4(1)^{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{7}]-\frac{4}{7}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{14}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{7}-\frac{4{x}^{7}}{49}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{8{e}^{14}}{7}-(\frac{4{e}^{14}}{49}-\frac{4}{49}) \\  & =\frac{1}{49}(56{e}^{14}-4{e}^{14}+4) \\  & =\frac{4}{49}(13{e}^{14}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 6
?

Calculate ∫xlog2⁡(3x)dx.

a
x22ln⁡2(ln⁡(3x)+2)+C
b
x4ln⁡2(2ln⁡(3x)+1)+C
c
x22ln⁡2(ln⁡(3x)−1)+C
d
x24ln⁡2(2ln⁡(3x)−1)+C
e
x22ln⁡2(xln⁡(3x)−2)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Change base to write log₂(3x)=ln(3x)/ln(2). Integration by parts with u=ln(3x) and dv=x dx gives [x²ln(3x)/2−x²/4]/ln(2)+C=x²(2ln(3x)−1)/(4ln(2))+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(3x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Question 6
?

Calculate ∫xlog2⁡(3x)dx.

a
x22ln⁡2(ln⁡(3x)+2)+C
b
x4ln⁡2(2ln⁡(3x)+1)+C
c
x22ln⁡2(ln⁡(3x)−1)+C
d
x24ln⁡2(2ln⁡(3x)−1)+C
e
x22ln⁡2(xln⁡(3x)−2)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log2⁡(3x)⟹u′=1xln⁡2v′=x⟹v=∫xdx=x22

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫xlog2⁡(3x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log2⁡(3x)⋅(x22)−∫(x22)(1xln⁡2)dx=x2log2⁡(3x)2−12ln⁡2∫xdx=x2ln⁡(3x)2ln⁡2−x24ln⁡2+C=x24ln⁡2(2ln⁡(3x)−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log2⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡2.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(3x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

before.html:
Question 7
?

Calculate ∫x2log2⁡(x)dx.

a
x39ln⁡2(3ln⁡x−1)+C
b
x29ln⁡2(3ln⁡x−1)+C
c
x33ln⁡2(ln⁡x−3)+C
d
x29ln⁡2(ln⁡x−3)+C
e
x33ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=log₂(x) and dv=x²dx gives du=dx/(x ln(2)) and v=x³/3. Thus the integral is x³ln(x)/(3ln(2))−x³/(9ln(2))+C=x³(3ln(x)−1)/(9ln(2))+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡(x))(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Question 7
?

Calculate ∫x2log2⁡(x)dx.

a
x39ln⁡2(3ln⁡x−1)+C
b
x29ln⁡2(3ln⁡x−1)+C
c
x33ln⁡2(ln⁡x−3)+C
d
x29ln⁡2(ln⁡x−3)+C
e
x33ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log2⁡(x)⟹u′=1xln⁡2v′=x2⟹v=∫x2dx=x33

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫x2log2⁡(x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=(log2⁡(x))(x33)−∫(x33)(1xln⁡2)dx=x3log2⁡(x)3−13ln⁡2∫x2dx=x3ln⁡x3ln⁡2−x39ln⁡2+C=x39ln⁡2(3ln⁡x−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log2⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. Integration by parts gives x³ln(x)/(3ln(2))−x³/(9ln(2))+C. Differentiating yields x²ln(x)/ln(2)=x²log₂(x), verifying the answer.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡(x))(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Calculate ∫xlog2⁡(x)dx.

a
 x2ln⁡2(4ln⁡x−1)+C
b
 x24ln⁡2(2ln⁡x−1)+C
c
 x22ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
d
 x24ln⁡2(4ln⁡x+1)+C
e
 x24ln⁡2(ln⁡x+1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using log₂(x)=ln(x)/ln(2), integration by parts gives x²ln(x)/(2ln(2))−x²/(4ln(2))+C=x²(2ln(x)−1)/(4ln(2))+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫25x4log2⁡(x)dx.

a
x5ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
b
5x4ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
c
x5ln⁡2(5ln⁡x−1)+C
d
5x5ln⁡2(5ln⁡x−1)+C
e
5x5ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=log₂(x) and dv=25x⁴dx gives du=dx/(x ln(2)) and v=5x⁵. Thus the integral is 5x⁵ln(x)/ln(2)−(5/ln(2))∫x⁴dx=x⁵(5ln(x)−1)/ln(2)+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=25{x}^{4}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(5{x}^{5})-\int \frac{5{x}^{5}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot {x}^{5}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫25x4log2⁡(x)dx.

a
x5ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
b
5x4ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
c
x5ln⁡2(5ln⁡x−1)+C
d
5x5ln⁡2(5ln⁡x−1)+C
e
5x5ln⁡2(ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log2⁡(x)⟹u′=1xln⁡2v′=25x4⟹v=∫25x4dx=5x5

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫25x4log2⁡(x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log2⁡(x)(5x5)−∫5x5xln⁡2dx=5x5log2⁡(x)−1ln⁡2∫5x4dx=5x5log2⁡(x)−1ln⁡2⋅x5+C=5x5ln⁡xln⁡2−x5ln⁡2+C=x5ln⁡2(5ln⁡x−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log2⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option c: integration by parts gives 5x⁵log₂(x)−x⁵/ln(2)+C=x⁵(5ln(x)−1)/ln(2)+C. Its derivative is 25x⁴ln(x)/ln(2)=25x⁴log₂(x).

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=25{x}^{4}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(5{x}^{5})-\int \frac{5{x}^{5}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot {x}^{5}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

before.html:
Question 10
?

Calculate ∫9x2log3⁡(2x)dx.

a
3x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)+1)+C
b
3x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
c
x3ln⁡3(3ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
d
9x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
e
x3ln⁡3(3ln⁡(2x)+1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=log₃(2x) and dv=9x²dx gives du=dx/(x ln(3)) and v=3x³. The integral is 3x³ln(2x)/ln(3)−x³/ln(3)+C=x³(3ln(2x)−1)/ln(3)+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (3{x}^{3})-\int \frac{3{x}^{3}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {x}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Question 10
?

Calculate ∫9x2log3⁡(2x)dx.

a
3x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)+1)+C
b
3x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
c
x3ln⁡3(3ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
d
9x3ln⁡3(ln⁡(2x)−1)+C
e
x3ln⁡3(3ln⁡(2x)+1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log3⁡(2x)⟹u′=1xln⁡3v′=9x2⟹v=∫9x2dx=3x3

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫9x2log3⁡(2x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log3⁡(2x)⋅(3x3)−∫3x3xln⁡3dx=3x3log3⁡(2x)−1ln⁡3∫3x2dx=3x3log3⁡(2x)−1ln⁡3⋅x3+C=3x3ln⁡(2x)ln⁡3−x3ln⁡3+C=x3ln⁡3(3ln⁡(2x)−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log3⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (3{x}^{3})-\int \frac{3{x}^{3}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {x}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

decision.explanation: Since log₂(x)=ln(x)/ln(2), integration by parts gives ∫log₂(x)dx=(x ln(x)−x)/ln(2)+C=x(ln(x)−1)/ln(2)+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(x){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-{\int }_{1}^{e}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e-x{|}_{1}^{e}\,] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}(e-e+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

∫ln⁡(x3)dx=

a
xln⁡(x3)−x+C
b
3xln⁡(x3)+x+C
c
xln⁡(x3)−3x+C
d

xln⁡(x3)−x3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write the integral as ∫ln⁡(x3)dx=∫ln⁡(x3)⋅1dx.

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(x3)⟹u′=1x3⋅3x2=3xv′=1⟹v=∫dx=x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫ln⁡(x3)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡(x3)⋅x−∫x⋅3xdx=xln⁡(x3)−3∫dx=xln⁡(x3)−3x+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

∫1/2e/2ln⁡(2x)dx=

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives the antiderivative x ln(2x)−x. At x=e/2 it equals 0, and at x=1/2 it equals −1/2. The integral is therefore 1/2.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/2}^{e/2}-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,(x){|}_{1/2}^{e/2}-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{e}{2})\,(\frac{e}{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{1}{2})\,(\frac{1}{2})]-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{e}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-x{|}_{1/2}^{e/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}e-\frac{1}{2}e+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(4x) and dv=2dx gives du=dx/x and v=2x. Thus the integral is 2x ln(4x)−∫2dx=2x(ln(4x)−1)+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x=2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =2\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-\int \,\text{d}x] \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-2x+C \\  & =2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

First, we write the integral as ∫2ln⁡4xdx=2∫ln⁡4x⋅1dx.

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(4x)⟹u′=1xv′=1⟹v=∫dx=x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 2∫ln⁡(4x)dx=2∫uv′dx=2[uv−∫vu′dx]=2[ln⁡(4x)⋅x−∫x⋅1xdx]=2[xln⁡(4x)−∫dx]=2xln⁡(4x)−2x+C=2x(ln⁡(4x)−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x=2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =2\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-\int \,\text{d}x] \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-2x+C \\  & =2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
